posts.head: Rwanda to Host F1’s Return to Africa, Will It Pay Off?
posts.text: Rwanda has been chosen to host Formula 1’s return to Africa, beating competition from South Africa and Morocco. With the first Grand Prix planned for the early 2030s, the country is betting on a new circuit, airport and hotels to drive tourism, create jobs and boost its economy. But can the benefits justify the cost? On Bloomberg’s Next Africa, Jennifer Zabasajja speaks to Rwanda’s Sports Minister Nelly Mukazayire about funding, jobs and the country’s sporting ambitions. posts.head: Almost 60% of primary energy used for electricity is lost to conversion and transmission
posts.text: In 2025, the United States consumed 34 quadrillion British thermal units (quads) of primary energy to deliver 14 quads of electricity sales to end users, with nearly 60% lost. About 95% of the losses came from converting primary energy into electricity, mostly due to lost heat from burning coal and natural gas. The remaining 5% was lost in the course of delivering electricity across grid infrastructure to homes and businesses.

posts.head: A Look at the Wider Divide in Credit Card Delinquency by Income
posts.text: Credit card delinquency rose sharply between 2022 and 2024, and the increase was steepest among borrowers in lower-income neighborhoods. Here, we check in on credit card performance by neighborhood income and trace when the borrowers who are now struggling with their payments were issued cards.
